10.1111/1475-679x.12053.title: The Impact of Recognition Versus Disclosure on Financial Information: A Preparer's Perspective
10.1111/1475-679x.12053.research_question: Does recognition versus footnote disclosure affect managers' contingent-liability estimates?
10.1111/1475-679x.12053.sample: Experiment with corporate controllers and CFOs at public and private companies; sample size and collection period not stated in abstract.
10.1111/1475-679x.12053.identification: Experiment varying recognition versus disclosure placement and comparing public- and private-company managers.
10.1111/1475-679x.12053.main_findings: Public-company managers expend more cognitive effort, exhibit less strategic bias, and report higher liability estimates under recognition than disclosure. The analogous placement effects are absent among private-company managers.

10.1016/j.jacceco.2014.08.007.title: Mandatory disclosure and asymmetry in financial reporting
10.1016/j.jacceco.2014.08.007.research_question: Why might managers collectively favor disclosure rules requiring more disclosure about adverse events?
10.1016/j.jacceco.2014.08.007.identification: Model of political influence in which a majority of informed managers chooses mandatory disclosure rules.
10.1016/j.jacceco.2014.08.007.main_findings: Equilibrium rules require greater disclosure of adverse events. Asymmetry increases with measurement informativeness, verifiability, and ex ante uncertainty.

10.2308/tar-2018-0262.title: Voluntary Disclosure Responses to Mandated Disclosure: Evidence from Australian Corporate Tax Transparency
10.2308/tar-2018-0262.research_question: How do firms supplement mandated public tax-return disclosures?
10.2308/tar-2018-0262.sample: Australian corporate tax-transparency setting; years and sample size not stated in abstract.
10.2308/tar-2018-0262.identification: Empirical analysis of supplemental voluntary disclosure around mandated tax disclosure; exact estimator not stated in abstract.
10.2308/tar-2018-0262.main_findings: Firms anticipating reputational costs from unexpectedly low disclosed tax liabilities issue preemptive and supplemental information, particularly when supplemental disclosure has low proprietary costs.

10.1007/s11142-026-09962-3.title: Tax numbers and ETR forecasting
10.1007/s11142-026-09962-3.research_question: What determines numeric tax disclosure, and how does it relate to analysts' implied ETR forecasts?
10.1007/s11142-026-09962-3.sample: Financial-statement tax disclosures; sample period and size not stated in abstract.
10.1007/s11142-026-09962-3.identification: Empirical analysis of disclosure determinants and forecast outcomes; causal identification not stated in abstract.
10.1007/s11142-026-09962-3.main_findings: More tax numbers are associated with lower implied ETR forecast errors and dispersion, particularly numbers in footnotes. Narrative emphasis does not provide the same reduction in information frictions.

10.1111/1475-679x.12617.title: Tax Strategy Disclosure: A Greenwashing Mandate?
10.1111/1475-679x.12617.research_question: Does mandated qualitative tax-strategy disclosure improve transparency and tax compliance?
10.1111/1475-679x.12617.sample: Large businesses affected by the 2016 UK tax-strategy disclosure reform; observation period and sample size not stated in abstract.
10.1111/1475-679x.12617.identification: Uses the 2016 UK reform as an exogenous disclosure shock; precise estimator not stated in abstract.
10.1111/1475-679x.12617.main_findings: Affected firms increase tax-strategy disclosure, but it becomes more boilerplate. The study finds no significant tax-planning response despite increased media attention.

10.1111/1475-679x.12151.title: Do PCAOB Inspections Improve the Quality of Internal Control Audits?
10.1111/1475-679x.12151.source: OpenAlex via search_journals; publisher abstract verified. Publisher assigns volume 55 to 2017; first online publication was September 12, 2016.

10.1111/1475-679x.12151.sample: U.S. internal-control audit and inspection setting; sample years and size not stated in abstract.

10.2308/ajpt-50752.main_findings: Audit firms lose significant market share following public disclosure of quality-control criticisms.

10.1093/rfs/hhad002.title: Climate Risk Disclosure and Institutional Investors
10.1093/rfs/hhad002.research_question: Do institutional investors demand and influence corporate climate-risk disclosure?
10.1093/rfs/hhad002.sample: Institutional-investor survey and observational holdings data; sample period and size not stated in abstract.
10.1093/rfs/hhad002.identification: Survey, holdings analyses, and a shock to French institutional investors' disclosure demand under Article 173.
10.1093/rfs/hhad002.main_findings: Investors report strong demand for climate disclosure and engagement. Climate-conscious ownership is positively associated with better disclosure, with additional evidence from the French demand shock.

10.2308/tar-2017-0550.title: Complementarity between Audited Financial Reporting and Voluntary Disclosure: The Case of Former Andersen Clients

10.2308/accr-51936.research_question: Does quarterly reporting affect banks' loan quality and risk-taking?

10.2308/accr-51936.identification: Examines banks switching to quarterly disclosure; precise estimator not stated in abstract.
10.2308/accr-51936.main_findings: Switching banks experience an approximately 11% relative decline in nonperforming loans and lower deposit rates and CDS spreads, consistent with market discipline.
